# Recreation Prompt

Recreate `Elemental Dex Dash`, a mobile-first portrait browser game built from a falling-object collector loop. Preserve the mechanics exactly: the player avatar stays near the bottom, follows horizontal touch/pointer input with lerp smoothing, falling entities spawn from the top, radius collisions resolve pickups or hazards, score rises by fixed category values, three lives determine failure, and restart resets the same loop.

Present the game as a bright creature-collector RPG route sprint. The player is a rookie trainer with an evolving starter aura. Common pickups are elemental motes worth Bond XP, rare creature pickups join a following team chain, rare dex flares grant a bigger bonus, and rival jammers remove hearts. Use cheerful procedural canvas art, rounded mobile HUD badges, readable portrait typography, elemental color motifs, and a sunny route background with light ambient motion.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a mobile canvas falling-object collector. The player avatar stays near the bottom, follows horizontal pointer/touch input, catches beneficial falling objects, avoids hazards, gains score, recruits followers, ramps difficulty by score, and reaches game over when three lives are lost.

## Protected mechanic truth
- One-axis drag/tap horizontal control.
- Continuous requestAnimationFrame update/draw loop.
- Falling spawn cadence tied to a score-based difficulty multiplier.
- Collision by player/item radius overlap.
- Reward categories: +100 common pickup, +500 companion pickup, +1000 rare bonus pickup.
- Hazard category removes one life; zero lives opens game-over and restart.
- Score thresholds change background phase and avatar evolution stage.

## Remixed identity
`Elemental Dex Dash` reframes the same loop as a bright creature-collector route dash. The trainer catches elemental motes, recruits wild mini-monsters into a following team, scans rare dex flares, and dodges rival jammers.

## Mobile-first target
Portrait-first canvas, readable HUD badges, one clear drag instruction, restart button with native click/tap behavior, and compact feedback that does not block the playfield.
